title: Mechanism Design for Honest AI: Testing Incentive-Compatible Reporting in LLMs

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether mechanism design tools from economics can improve LLM honesty without internal access. If proper scoring rule prompting improves calibration, this provides a practical and theoretically grounded technique for eliciting honest AI behavior.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompting an existing LLM with different elicitation strategies and measuring calibration error is highly accessible. No model training required. ECE computation is straightforward. CS beginners can execute this with minimal mentor support. Compute requirements are minimal (inference only).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three prompting strategies, same prediction tasks, measure ECE for each. Clear deliverable: calibration comparison table. Can be completed well within 30 hours. No training, no complex infrastructure.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
